Entropy-weighted imbalance: Compute the Shannon entropy of the bid/ask size distribution across all 5 levels separately for Up and Down tokens in the first 5 seconds. Low entropy (concentrated liquidity at one level) combined with directional imbalance may signal informed positioning, while high entropy (diffuse liquidity) suggests noise — use the entropy ratio between Up and Down books as a confidence-weighted signal that filters out low-conviction imbalance readings.

Cross-token spread divergence: In the first 1-5 seconds, compute the spread on both the Up token book and the Down token book simultaneously. When one token's spread tightens while the other's widens, it signals asymmetric market-maker confidence in a direction — the token with the tighter spread is attracting competitive quoting because makers believe it will resolve favorably. Use the signed spread difference (spread_Down - spread_Up) as the predictor, potentially combined with a minimum absolute divergence threshold to filter noise.

Level-weighted imbalance acceleration: Instead of static imbalance, compute imbalance at two ultra-short windows (0-2s and 2-5s post-open) using inverse-level weighting (L5 weight=5, L4=4, ..., L1=1) to emphasize deeper book activity that is harder to spoof. The second derivative (acceleration of this deep-book imbalance) captures whether informed flow is building or fading — positive acceleration toward the bid side predicts Up resolution, and a magnitude threshold filters out markets where early flow is ambiguous or mean-reverting.
